natural_body: 40% SMB discount: signup +31%, revenue +18%, but retention -12%; no renewal.

first.rationale:
The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point directly at the funnel stage that memory_86 and memory_31 both claim to move, and those are the only two memories that speak to a durable lift rather than a one-quarter bump. That is exactly why I am spending the verification budget on them rather than on the memory I plan to reject: memory_73 already tells me promotional pricing bought signup and revenue at the cost of retention with no renewal, and pulling its source record would only confirm a direction I am not taking. Verification is worth more spent on the load-bearing evidence for the action I intend than on the evidence for the action I have already ruled out. Competitor entry pricing is real pressure, but matching it would trade sustainable qualified revenue for churn-prone volume, which contradicts the primary objective.

What I specifically want from the archive: memory_31 is from day 12 and memory_86 from day 52, and both are consolidated summaries whose original records I have not seen. I want to know whether they are two independent findings or one effect described twice, what 'durable' meant in measurement window terms, and whether the lift was measured on activation itself or only on completion rates. If they turn out to be the same underlying experiment re-consolidated, my evidence base is half as strong as it looks and I should size down accordingly.

Risk I am carrying forward: memory_31's mechanism is cutting required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise converts better through sales-assisted, demo-request paths that depend on qualifying information. Stripping fields to fix SMB activation could quietly degrade enterprise pipeline quality, which is the higher-value revenue stream. So this runs as a standard experiment with segment-split treatment (self-serve SMB only, enterprise path untouched), and I want retention and pipeline-quality readouts alongside the activation lift, not activation alone. Referral incentive (memory_57) stays the fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding evidence, since it added qualified revenue without retention harm, but it does not address the metric that is actually declining.
